general.title: Everybody’s Business: China Is Writing Its Own AI Playbook
general.summary: While US AI companies are struggling with a public image problem, Chinese attitudes towards AI are generally more positive with the government leading the charge to turn its rural and inland regions into AI-driven manufacturing hubs. Brad Stone joins Stacey Vanek Smith and Max Chafkin on the Everybody’s Business podcast to discuss his factory tour of EV maker Zeekr and how China is writing its own AI story. (Source: Bloomberg)

general.title: Fed Set to Raise Interest Rates Next Month as Debate Moves to January
general.summary: The US monetary policy debate has already moved on to January.

general.title: Centrica, Equinor in Next Round of Germany’s Uniper Sale
general.summary: Centrica Plc and Equinor ASA are among companies advancing to the second round of the sale process for Germany’s Uniper SE, according to people familiar with the matter.

general.title: Ackman on Huang's Exit, Anthropic IPO Roadshow
general.summary: Bill Ackman, Pershing Square founder and CEO, says it's sad to see Jensen Huang leave Nvidia and he'll go on to do something great. Ackman also says he was impressed with the presentation given by Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei at the company's IPO roadshow event in New York. He speaks to Bloomberg's Isabelle Lee. (Source: Bloomberg)

general.title: Anthropic CEO Calls Computing Power Deepest Business Dilemma
general.summary: Anthropic PBC Chief Executive Officer Dario Amodei named sourcing computing power as one of the artificial intelligence company’s biggest challenges, in a briefing ahead of its hotly anticipated initial public offering.

general.title: Amazon Forced Into First North American Union Pact in Canada
general.summary: Hundreds of Amazon.com Inc. warehouse employees in western Canada are the company’s first North American logistics workers to be covered by a union contract after an independent arbitrator on Friday imposed terms between the online retailer and Unifor, one of the largest private-sector unions in the nation.

general.title: Nagel Says ‘Highly Probable’ That ECB Will Have to Act Again
general.summary: European Central Bank Governing Council member Joachim Nagel said it’s very likely that borrowing costs will have to be raised further due to upward pressure on consumer prices.

general.title: Russian Economy Slows as Ukrainian Strikes Weigh on Output
general.summary: Russia’s economy slowed in the third quarter as Ukrainian attacks knocked out industrial facilities, disrupted logistics and added to inflationary pressures.

general.title: Fed’s Logan Calls for Clearer Separation of Market Operations
general.summary: Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas President Lorie Logan said the US central bank should separate assets purchased for market-functioning purposes from the ones it holds for monetary-policy operations in order to more clearly communicate its intentions during periods of financial stress.

general.title: Cisco beats on earnings, says AI infrastructure revenue will double this fiscal year
general.summary: Cisco is trying to become a bigger player in AI after missing out on the early years of the boom.

general.title: Goolsbee Says Fed Must Reestablish Its Inflation Credibility
general.summary: Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago President Austan Goolsbee said the US central bank must take more action to bring down inflation.

general.title: Bessent Blames Lutnick, Commerce for Not Blocking Megaspeed
general.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said his agency had long supported putting Megaspeed International on a trade blacklist but that responsibility for doing so rested with Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick.

general.title: US Wholesale Inflation Picks Up to Fastest Pace Since 2022
general.summary: US wholesale inflation climbed in October from a year earlier at the fastest pace since 2022, adding to evidence of persistent price pressures throughout the economy.

general.title: Merz Says German Proposal for Top ECB Jobs Coming Next Week
general.summary: Germany will make a suggestion in the coming days for a package to fill three top European Central Bank positions, including that of President Christine Lagarde.

general.title: U.S. seizes $1.2 billion in cryptocurrency stolen from Binance
general.summary: The DOJ said it was taking action against the North Korean government's "schemes to fund its regime through the massive theft of cryptocurrency."

general.title: The US Job Market Narrative Shifts Toward Inflationary Risks
general.summary: Labor hasn’t been a source of price pressure for years, but that could change.

general.title: Private Credit, Stablecoins Pose Risks Beyond Size, Bailey Warns
general.summary: Private credit and stablecoins could become systemic risks before they achieve systemic size, Bank of England governor Andrew Bailey warned on Friday, signaling that global policymakers should continue to be vigilant on those corners of global finance.

general.title: German Lawmakers Sign Off on Higher Borrowing, Spending for 2027
general.summary: German lawmakers signed off on a spending plan for 2027 that entails borrowing and spending that exceed initial estimates as the country ratchets up investment into infrastructure and an expanding military.

general.title: Jim Cramer has three lingering questions about Anthropic ahead of its historic IPO
general.summary: Jim Cramer identified three lingering questions about Anthropic ahead of its highly anticipated IPO.
